reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker favorably endorses BitClub Network and tells viewers they can invest through paid cloud-mining pool options. The presentation solicits pool purchases and registration by citing mining commissions and daily or personal bitcoin results. It also promotes a high-value founder package with pools, tokens, and coins as payment for claimed crypto returns.

citations.quote: The first pool can be $ 500, other $ 1000 and the third $ 2000.
For investors who invest money to purchase the equipment they create the company and give a pool.
you will be able to receive 50 percent on it commissions from the extracted currency
The first pool brings 48 thousand Satoshi per day.
in case you decide to invest in this company, or be its partner

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker's confidence should not be mistaken for an unconditional promise. He frames the question of joining as something viewers may ask, then offers his opinion about the company's prospects: “you ask me whether it is too late or not too late come here? Certainly not too late” (ASR_0006). He also describes investing as the viewer's decision, saying “in case you decide to invest in this company, or be its partner” (ASR_0009). Those qualifications do not erase the favorable commentary, but they matter: the cited language offers a personal investment view, not a guarantee that every viewer will earn the amounts discussed.

citations.quote: you ask me whether it is too late or not too late come here? Certainly not too late
in case you decide to invest in this company, or be its partner

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening points to pool prices and a stated commission rate, but a price and a commission description do not themselves promise a fixed payout. Its daily figure is introduced as the speaker's own example: “The first pool brings 48 thousand Satoshi per day” (ASR_0005). And the cited invitation says “in case you decide,” preserving the viewer's choice (ASR_0009). The prosecution has shown an optimistic account of an investment, not an explicit assurance that the reported result will recur for a new buyer.

citations.quote: The first pool brings 48 thousand Satoshi per day.
in case you decide to invest in this company, or be its partner

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the purchase optional does not change what is being offered. The speaker names paid pools and then ties them to mining income: “The first pool can be $ 500, other $ 1000 and the third $ 2000” (ASR_0003), while “you will be able to receive 50 percent on it commissions from the extracted currency” (ASR_0004). He goes beyond a tentative forecast by saying “I am sure that you can invest in this company” (ASR_0008). No guaranteed return is required to recognize promotion of paid mining returns.

citations.quote: The first pool can be $ 500, other $ 1000 and the third $ 2000.
you will be able to receive 50 percent on it commissions from the extracted currency
I am sure that you can invest in this company

opening.argument: Judge, consider the presentation's central activity. The description calls it “A complete review of the company” (DESCRIPTION_0001). The speaker promises to move to the screen and show how the site works (ASR_0001), then walks through mining-pool information and an outside pool listing (ASR_0003). He also shows a wallet transaction page (F0030). This is a narrated examination of a platform and the speaker's experience with it. The favorable conclusions deserve scrutiny, but describing purchase options during a review does not, by itself, make the video an instruction to send money.

citations.quote: A complete review of the company
Now we'll move to the monitor screen I will record from the screen and you will be able to see how you can do your investment.
Let's go to the Blockchain website itself

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution quotes prices, commissions and a daily figure, but those are also the details a review of a paid mining service would examine. The speaker says he will “tell you step-by-step” (ASR_0002), and the displayed transaction page supplies context for his account (F0030); it does not independently establish that a new purchaser will receive the same result. The quoted invitation to contact him if someone decides to invest does not turn every preceding demonstration into a purchase instruction.

citations.quote: I'll try to give you this brief review and tell you step-by-step

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough includes a direct sales path: the displayed pool options have purchase buttons (F0024), and the speaker says viewers will be shown “how you can do your investment” (ASR_0001). His conclusion is not neutral evaluation; he says “I am sure that you can invest in this company” (ASR_0008). The transaction screen may illustrate his account, but it does not verify the promised mining returns or remove the promotional force of the paid-pool presentation.

citations.quote: you will be able to see how you can do your investment
I am sure that you can invest in this company

opening.argument: Judge, the offer is presented as a mining service with stated prices, not as an unexplained transfer of funds. The speaker says investors' money is used “to purchase the equipment” (ASR_0003), and the site displays separate pool options with prices and purchase buttons (F0024). He also discusses a physical wallet that customers could order (ASR_0009). These commercial details do not prove the service delivers what it claims. They do, however, leave an important evidentiary gap: the cited material shows an advertised service and reported results, not proof that buyers' funds are diverted or that the displayed transactions are fabricated.

citations.quote: For investors who invest money to purchase the equipment they create the company and give a pool.
you can order yourself such wallet, or you can order a large batch

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution establishes that pool purchases and mining-related payments are advertised. It does not establish that the equipment-purchase account is false: the speaker explicitly describes investors funding equipment (ASR_0003). Nor does his report of a daily amount prove that every buyer is promised that amount; he introduces it within his own pool example (ASR_0005). The evidence supports examining the offer critically, but not treating an unproven diversion of funds as an observed fact.

citations.quote: For investors who invest money to purchase the equipment they create the company and give a pool.
The first pool brings 48 thousand Satoshi per day.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is the promoted mechanism, not whether this video independently proves where every payment goes. Viewers are offered paid mining pools (F0024), and the speaker links them to commissions “from the extracted currency” (ASR_0004) and a daily Satoshi amount (ASR_0005). A separate wallet product does not change the purpose of the pool purchase. The defense's missing-proof argument overlooks that the speaker actively encourages investment in the paid return-bearing offer.
